# legal-ai-agent

> Open-source FastAPI service that reviews contracts, appeals, and legal documents, powered by Claude Opus 4.8. Returns extracted clauses, risks, compliance flags, recommendations, a deterministic 0-100 safety score with an A-F letter grade, and a 0-100 overall-confidence score. Every finding ships with a verbatim citation that the server anchors to source character-for-character — findings whose citations are not present verbatim are auto-downgraded to low confidence. The model proposes; the server verifies at the source level, which makes hallucinated findings structurally impossible to score well.

License: MIT. Repository: https://github.com/dnzengou/legal-ai-agent. Live demo: https://legal-ai-agent.netlify.app.

## What it does

- Ingests contracts as text (`POST /review`) or base64-encoded PDF (`POST /review-pdf`).
- Extracts parties, effective date, term, and key clauses (termination, indemnification, LoL, IP, confidentiality, payment, governing law, dispute resolution, auto-renewal, assignment, change of control) with character-offset citations into the source.
- Flags risks by severity (low · medium · high) with verbatim excerpts.
- Flags per-framework compliance status (GDPR · CCPA · HIPAA · PCI-DSS · SOC 2 · others the contract implicates).
- Produces actionable recommendations for the reviewing party.
- Computes `safety_score` (0-100), `letter_grade` (A-F), `overall_confidence` (0-100), and `confidence_level` (high/medium/low) deterministically server-side — the model cannot inflate them.

## How it prevents hallucination

Every `Risk` and every non-`not_applicable` `ComplianceFlag` must carry a `provenance.text_excerpt` — a verbatim quote from the source (≤500 chars). The server performs exact-substring anchoring. If the quote is not present character-for-character, the finding's `confidence` is forcibly downgraded to `low`, which drags down `overall_confidence`. There is no way for the model to score well with a fabricated citation. The landing-page demo shows the glass-box: cited findings get a green ✓ badge with the quoted excerpt; unanchored findings show as "no verbatim citation".
